audit_organization: Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)
report_title: Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India on Direct Benefit Transfer Schemes in Tamil Nadu
finding_summary: Direct benefit transfer roll-out successfully credited 1.065 crore women beneficiaries in maiden month; audit observed minor transaction failure rates due to unlinked Aadhaar-bank NPCI mapper entries in rural cooperative accounts.
documented_implementation_gap: Initial delay in grievance disposal for 1.85 lakh rejected applicants appealing through revenue divisional officer appeal portal.
documented_financial_observation: Total disbursement of Rs 7,995.12 Crore in FY 2023-24 reconciled against State Treasury sub-head with negligible unspent balance (Rs 1.88 Crore returned to consolidated fund).
recommendation: Establish mandatory automated SMS notification for uncredited payments and institutionalize time-bound 15-day appellate grievance disposal.
department_response: Department accepted recommendation; integrated real-time NPCI mapping validation portal and notified 30-day statutory appeal disposal standard.

audit_organization: Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)
report_title: Report of the CAG on General and Social Sector, Government of Tamil Nadu (Report No. 3 of 2024)
finding_summary: Pudhumai Penn incentive successfully expanded higher education enrollment; audit observed need for automated semester attendance verification between colleges and Social Welfare portal to prevent payments after student dropouts.
documented_implementation_gap: Manual attendance certificate collection in self-financing arts colleges led to 14 to 30 day payment lag in second semester disbursements.
documented_financial_observation: Disbursements of Rs 698.00 Crore fully expended with zero diversion of funds to other social welfare sub-heads.
recommendation: Integrate State Higher Education Council ERP with TN e-Governance Agency for automated monthly attendance data feeds.
department_response: API integration between EMIS, College ERPs, and e-Governance portal commissioned in academic year 2023-24.
evidence_locator: Chapter II, Performance Audit Paragraph 2.8, Pages 45-49

audit_organization: State Planning Commission, Government of Tamil Nadu
report_title: Mid-Term Evaluation Study of Makkalai Thedi Maruthuvam Healthcare Delivery Model
finding_summary: Independent sample survey across 12 districts confirmed 83.4% of surveyed chronic patients received regular monthly anti-hypertensive and anti-diabetic drug kits at doorstep without out-of-pocket payment.
documented_implementation_gap: Supply-chain stockouts of secondary hypertension drugs (e.g. Telmisartan) recorded in 6 remote tribal primary health centers in Nilgiris and Dindigul.
documented_financial_observation: Procurement expenditure through Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation (TNMSC) maintained at 12% lower unit cost than open market retail.
recommendation: Institute buffer inventory at block primary health centers and equip health volunteers with automated low-stock alert apps.
department_response: TNMSC buffer stock threshold increased from 30 to 60 days in hilly and remote block PHCs.

audit_organization: State Planning Commission, Government of Tamil Nadu
report_title: Impact Assessment of the Chief Minister Breakfast Scheme in Primary Schools
finding_summary: Comprehensive evaluation in 1,545 pilot schools documented average 8.4% increase in student attendance, with 12.8% surge in municipal school attendance; 92% of headmasters reported improved first-period student engagement.
documented_implementation_gap: Centralized kitchen transit delays during rainy days in Chennai Corporation led to breakfast serving beyond 8:45 AM cutoff in 14 schools.
documented_financial_observation: Per-child per-meal cost verified at Rs 12.71 including vegetable procurement, liquefied petroleum gas, and self-help group honorarium.
recommendation: Decentralize cooking clusters to neighborhood school clusters and mandate thermal container transport.
department_response: Procured insulated transport boxes and established 35 new sub-zonal kitchen clusters in Chennai.

audit_organization: Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)
report_title: Report of the CAG on Local Bodies (Government of Tamil Nadu) — Performance of Solid Waste Management
finding_summary: Audit evaluated biomining contracts at Perungudi and Kodungaiyur dumpsites; noted positive clearance of legacy waste but flagged delays in setting up regional waste-to-energy incineration facilities.
documented_implementation_gap: Source segregation at household level remained uneven across municipal zones (achieved 54% vs mandated 100% under Solid Waste Rules 2016).
documented_financial_observation: Capital utilization under Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban) / State Urban Development Fund stood at 78% of sanctioned outlays.
recommendation: Strictly enforce decentralized wet waste processing and mandate biometric attendance for mechanized street sweeping contractors.
department_response: GCC deployed RFID-tagged waste bin monitoring and expanded micro-composting centers across all 15 zones.
evidence_locator: Chapter III: Urban Local Bodies Audit, Paragraph 3.4, Pages 85-98
